components.css: :host{--bay:#0E0E10;--panel:#1A1A1E;--track:#2A2A30;--track-hi:#34343B;--line:#3A3A42;--paper:#F4F1EA;--dim:#A9A59C;--ink:#0E0E10;--cut:#FF3B2F;--cut-text:#FF5A4F;--marker:#F5D90A;--clip-com:#F28C38;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--display:'Clash Display','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;--body:'General Sans',-apple-system,Arial,sans-serif}.ds-btn-sec{background:transparent;color:var(--paper);font:500 13px var(--mono);height:48px;padding:0 16px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:3px;cursor:pointer}.ds-btn-sec:hover{border-color:var(--paper)}.ds-btn-sec:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--cut);outline-offset:2px}

components.css: :host{--bay:#0E0E10;--panel:#1A1A1E;--track:#2A2A30;--track-hi:#34343B;--line:#3A3A42;--paper:#F4F1EA;--dim:#A9A59C;--ink:#0E0E10;--cut:#FF3B2F;--cut-text:#FF5A4F;--marker:#F5D90A;--clip-com:#F28C38;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--display:'Clash Display','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;--body:'General Sans',-apple-system,Arial,sans-serif}.ds-ws{display:flex;gap:2px;background:var(--bay);padding:0 8px;height:36px}.ds-ws button{background:var(--panel);color:var(--dim);border:0;padding:0 16px;font:500 12px var(--mono);letter-spacing:.04em;text-transform:uppercase;cursor:pointer}.ds-ws button:hover{color:var(--paper)}.ds-ws button[aria-current=page]{background:var(--track);color:var(--paper);box-shadow:inset 0 2px 0 var(--cut)}.ds-ws .ds-contact{margin-left:auto;background:var(--cut);color:var(--ink);font-weight:700}.ds-ws .ds-contact:hover{background:var(--cut-text)}.ds-ws button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--cut);outline-offset:-2px}

components.css: :host{--bay:#0E0E10;--panel:#1A1A1E;--track:#2A2A30;--track-hi:#34343B;--line:#3A3A42;--paper:#F4F1EA;--dim:#A9A59C;--ink:#0E0E10;--cut:#FF3B2F;--cut-text:#FF5A4F;--marker:#F5D90A;--clip-com:#F28C38;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--display:'Clash Display','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;--body:'General Sans',-apple-system,Arial,sans-serif}.ds-field{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;width:280px}.ds-field span{font:500 11px var(--mono);letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--dim)}.ds-field input{height:48px;background:var(--track);color:var(--paper);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:2px;padding:10px 12px;font:14px var(--mono)}.ds-field input:focus{outline:none;border:2px solid var(--cut);padding:9px 11px}

components.css: :host{--bay:#0E0E10;--panel:#1A1A1E;--track:#2A2A30;--track-hi:#34343B;--line:#3A3A42;--paper:#F4F1EA;--dim:#A9A59C;--ink:#0E0E10;--cut:#FF3B2F;--cut-text:#FF5A4F;--marker:#F5D90A;--clip-com:#F28C38;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;--display:'Clash Display','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;--body:'General Sans',-apple-system,Arial,sans-serif}.ds-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:160px minmax(0,1fr) auto;gap:16px;align-items:center;width:640px;padding:8px;background:var(--panel);color:var(--paper);border:0;border-top:4px solid var(--c);border-radius:3px;text-align:left;cursor:pointer}.ds-row:hover{box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--marker)}.ds-row:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--paper);outline-offset:-2px}.ds-th{aspect-ratio:16/9;background:#000;position:relative}.ds-th b{position:absolute;left:4px;top:4px;background:var(--bay);color:var(--paper);font:500 11px var(--mono);padding:1px 5px}.ds-tx{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:2px;min-width:0}.ds-t{font:500 13px var(--mono)}.ds-s{font:12px var(--mono);color:var(--dim)}.ds-d{font:14px/1.5 var(--body);color:var(--dim);display:-webkit-box;-webkit-line-clamp:2;-webkit-box-orient:vertical;overflow:hidden}.ds-rt{font:12px var(--mono);color:var(--dim);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}

components.name: Label Chip
components.description: Any label that sits on a poster or film strip.

narrative.overview: The site is Cindy's edit bay: a full-screen editing app with an app bar, workspace tabs, a project bin, a program monitor, an inspector, a timeline with audio meters, and a status strip. Every editor detail is real. The bay is for the work, not about the interface: the program monitor is the largest object on every screen, and each editor word has a plain word with it. The surface is dark, flat, and dense, like a real NLE at night.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, flat panels with 2px bay seams between them.
The program monitor leads; panels are slim at rest.
Editor language with a plain partner on every label.
Category color is the wayfinding system, used the same way everywhere.
Motion is counted in frames at 24 fps.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Razor Red means the cut or the primary action. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Color Is a Category Rule
rules.body: The four clip colors mark categories and nothing else. A category keeps its color on every page.

rules.name: The Banned Pairs Rule
rules.body: Never paper on cut (3.15:1). Never cut as small text on track (4.02:1); use cut-text on panel. Never faint as text.

rules.name: The Text Floor Rule
rules.body: No functional text under 11px on desktop or 12px on phone. That includes ruler labels, track ids, pin labels, and canvas text.

rules.name: The Mono Is Interface Rule
rules.body: Mono sets interface, not prose. Any paragraph longer than two lines uses Body.

rules.name: The Monitor Leads Rule
rules.body: On every screen, the program monitor or the page's main picture is the largest object. If a panel competes with it, the panel collapses.

rules.name: The Plain Partner Rule
rules.body: Every editor label has a plain label next to it or under it: "Export (send)" with "Send message", "V1 Pages" with "Pages", "Yellow pins = feedback rounds".

rules.name: The Thumb Wins Rule
rules.body: On phone, every tap target is at least 44 × 44px. When a desktop height is smaller (the 26px app bar, the 30px ruler, 44px tracks), the phone version grows to fit the target.

rules.name: The Seam Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Panels separate with 2px bay seams. Never add a shadow to a panel or a card.

dos: Do keep the program monitor the largest object on every screen (min(100%, calc(64vh * 16 / 9)) on desktop).
Do put a plain label with every editor word ("Export (send)" + "Send message").
Do put every label that sits on an image on a solid bay label chip.
Do load video only on click, and show a poster before that.
Do keep J/K/L as in Premiere (back, pause, play) and use arrows for clips.
Do keep touch targets at 44px on phone and at least 24px on desktop.
Do use the CBC mark in the app bar.
Do write "Adobe Media Encoder" in the tools list.
donts: Don't show an Apple logo or any OS logo.
Don't put instruction text ("Press L for sound…") in the hero or on phone.
Don't set functional text under 11px (12px on phone), or use Tick Gray as text.
Don't add shadows to panels, rows, or cards.
Don't let Space or Enter do anything but press the focused control.
Don't let a note or tooltip run past the app frame.
Don't start video or a download on hover.
Don't use pills, gradients on surfaces, or color that does not carry a meaning.
